    • The Israeli startup, founded in 2023, is best known for its software that lets developers sync their AI models across different chips, allowing them to switch hardware rapidly, known as the Decart Optimization Stack.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Amazon is scooping up much of the technology and talent behind artificial intelligence startup Decart, marking the latest reverse acquihire deal by a major tech company.

    In a Monday blog post, Amazon said it agreed to purchase Decart's "proprietary technology" and hire the startup's three founders, as well as their AI researchers and engineers.

    The Israeli startup, founded in 2023, is best known for its software that lets developers sync their AI models across different chips, allowing them to switch hardware rapidly, known as the Decart Optimization Stack.

    "Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip," Peter DeSantis, a senior vice president at Amazon who oversees foundation models, custom silicon and quantum computing development, stated in a statement. "More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.".

    DeSantis added, "From our earliest work with Decart, we knew they were the kind of technologically fearless team who would help us push it even further.".

    Sources indicate that amazon has moved deeper into building custom AI chips amid insatiable demand for the technology, and as companies seek alternatives to Nvidia, the dominant provider. Amazon has positioned its Trainium and Inferentia chips as lower-cost options for AI developers.

    Last month, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said the company plans to make its Trainium chips externally available for the first time in "late in 2027.".

    Several outlets reported Amazon will pay $7.5 billion for Decart's assets, citing people familiar with the matter. Amazon declined to comment on the terms of the deal.

    Anthropic had considered acquiring Decart and conducted due diligence, but ultimately walked away from a deal, Bloomberg reported.

    Recent findings suggest that tech companies including Microsoft, Meta and Google have announced a series of deals with buzzy AI startups, which involve licensing their technology or nabbing their top talent and founders. The moves, often referred to as reverse acquihires, stop short of buying the companies outright. Amazon made two similar deals in 2024 when it brought on talent from Adept and Covariant.

    It has been revealed that the arrangements have attracted regulatory scrutiny in some cases. Amazon mentioned Monday the Decart deal is subject to regulatory approval.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the organization "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    Recent findings suggest that the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also said that newly introduced export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    Industry observers note that "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson remarked in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Industry observers note that lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "key" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    SpaceX sued by Oregon and Virginia over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the company over issues with its Grok AI image generator.
    • Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled people to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation, the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others.
    • In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X users from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the company over issues with its Grok AI image generator.

    Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled people to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation, the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others.

    In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X users from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

    Sources indicate that the complaints also allege that SpaceX has falsely represented its AI apps and social network (Grok and X) as generally safe, which the states see as a violation of Virginia's Consumer Protection Act or Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. The matter is particularly concerning because X allows minors 13 and older to access its content.

    Rayfield and Jones both noted in their complaints that harms caused by non-consensual, sexualized images go beyond the victims depicted in the images.

    "This content can cause fear, distress, and anxiety in those who are unwillingly exposed to the content," Jones wrote. Rayfield wrote that such conduct "erodes important norms regarding consent and privacy and trivializes sexual imagery, abuse, and exploitation.".

    In a statement emailed to CNBC by a spokesperson for SpaceXSI, and posted on the company's @Safety account on X, the company stated, "When someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content, we take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement. Attempting to create this material is a serious crime, and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors.".

    At an NYC Council hearing in October, a SpaceX AI policy leader, Gabriela Castillo Madrid, said the tech giant had appropriate "safeguards" and "strict controls" in place around its AI products.

    SpaceX was already facing multiple Grok- and X-related lawsuits, and government probes around the world, including by authorities in the U.K., Spain, Ireland, France and the state of California.

    Industry observers note that in private-sector lawsuits filed against SpaceX in the U.S. concerning Grok and AI-generated, explicit images, litigation is still in early stages and is tracked by The Center for Internet Technology Addiction.

    It has been revealed that when the city of Baltimore sued xAI, now owned and operated by SpaceX, the organization argued that under Section 230, they were not liable for unwanted images. Section 230 is a federal law that largely shields online platforms from liability for users' content.

    According to recent reports, spaceX also sued a user in a federal court in the Northern District of Texas for breach of contract after he allegedly used Grok to create and distribute deepfake explicit images, including depictions of minors. Lawyers for Musk's company argued that Grok should be seen as "a neutral tool, subject to user control," and that any image generation "is the result of the user's prompts and directions.".

    The upcoming state suits add to legal pressure on SpaceX. Both Virginia and Oregon are seeking injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs, while Virginia is also seeking restitution for consumers from Musk's tech giant.

    Oregon submitted its complaint to the Multnomah County Circuit Court on Sunday evening, and Virginia submitted its complaint to the City of Richmond Circuit Court Monday morning. As of early Monday, the suits were pending the courts' acceptance.

    State attorneys general have recently succeeded in compelling U.S. social media companies to change their products and pay for alleged past harms.

    In August, for example, Meta settled a major federal case centered on allegations that the social media giant misrepresented the level of child mental health problems caused by its apps, Facebook and Instagram. Without admitting to wrongdoing, Meta agreed to pay states around $17 billion over a 10-year period and to make app changes that experts believe will help keep children safer online.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, sharply reversing Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020.
    • Recent findings suggest that shares of Nvidia surged 31.48% after the manufacturer unveiled Monday morning that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.
    • Nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement followed a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, sharply reversing Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020.

    Recent findings suggest that shares of Nvidia surged 31.48% after the manufacturer unveiled Monday morning that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO. The semiconductor giant gained back nearly $1 trillion in market cap, posting its best day since May 2003.

    Nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement followed a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month. The company has been embattled as reports surfaced about Huang's multiple extramarital affairs — one of which was with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang resigned as CEO of the company he founded on Nov. 12.

    Industry observers note that the Nasdaq Composite surged 6.51% Monday, for its best day since April 9, 2025. The Nasdaq slid 10% last week, with tech stocks having a rocky week as investors remained nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models. All three major averages ended last week in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026.

    Shares of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade saw a lift Monday on the Nvidia news.

    It has been revealed that shares of Alphabet surged 6.34%, Meta gained 6.55%, Amazon jumped 3.47% and Microsoft increased 1.65%. SpaceX added 4.35%, Arm Holdings surged 16.08% and AMD added 6.85%. Dell and Micron posted some of the sector's biggest gains of the day, gaining 20.46% and 19.04%, respectively. The iShares Semiconductor ETF gained 13.63%.

    Neoclouds, which have seen a particularly choppy few months amid AI boom financing concerns, surged on Huang's reinstatement. Nebius soared 20.28%, CoreWeave gained 22.32% and Iren gained 23.86%.

    Recent findings suggest that following a brief premarket surge, Anthropic shares posted a decline of 1.43% in its third day of trading. Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, before closing down 8.5% on Friday.

    Speaking to CNBC's Eamon Javers about Huang's reinstatement, President Donald Trump on Monday mentioned that last week's market sell-off "probably" influenced his support for the ousted CEO's return.

    According to recent reports, "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was, he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about," Trump stated on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street.".

    Trump mentioned he spoke to Nvidia's board directly and that he "convinced" the board to reinstate Huang, who the president said "did nothing wrong.".

    Industry observers note that "That thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taking the whole market with it," Trump said, referring to Nvidia's stock price.

    "The board was in a bad position, but they were put in an easier position to do this when the stock lost 50% of its value or whatever the number was," the president mentioned.

    It's Thanksgiving week in the NBA and looking back, fantasy basketball managers have plenty to be thankful for (if they were able to avoid the injury bug after the first month-plus of the 2026-27 season).

    Sources indicate that in Yahoo High Score fantasy basketball, it was a pretty eventful Week 5 with a few 50-burgers and three players landing in the perfect lineup thanks to an overtime track meet between the Bulls and Nuggets on Sunday. Let's dive into the perfect lineup and break down the top performers.

    Week 5 High Score perfect lineup.

    Josh Giddey: The Bulls guard had been off to a slow start to the season, averaging just 8.5 points and 7.5 assists per game in six contests in the opening month. But since November came along, Giddey has upped his game a bit, though managers would like to see him be more aggressive on offense. But that unselfishness is why Giddey landed in the perfect lineup, posting 23 points, 14 rebounds and 22 assists for 84 fantasy points in the Bulls' OT loss to Denver on Sunday. Chicago has three gettable matchups in Week 6, so be sure to get Giddey in those lineups.

    It has been revealed that jamal Murray: The Nuggets' guard is pacing toward his best NBA season, averaging 26.2 points per game after Sunday's 45-point outburst in the win over Chicago. That point-per-minute performance awarded Murray 79 fantasy points and one of the guard spots in the perfect lineup. Murray also chipped in 5 rebounds, 7 assists and 5 stocks — pretty good category coverage. A consensus second-round pick preseason, Murray is looking like an early league-winner if he can keep this up.

    Recent findings suggest that victor Wembanyama: Wow, we didn't expect Wemby to land in this article again (wink). But really, Wembanyama is putting together an MVP campaign so far in 2026-27, and has been arguably the best asset for High Score fantasy basketball (Luka Dončić is really the only one ahead of him right now). After last week's 50-point outing against the Pelicans, Wembanyama now has the two highest single outputs of the season for High Score (110, 97). He'll get another shot to try and top the High Score leaderboard in Week 6 with four games on tap.

    In a recent development, nikola Jokić: The Joker benefitted from that overtime contest on Sunday, same as Giddey and Murray. It was the Nuggets significant's second-highest fantasy score of the season with a 37-18-11 triple-double, just his fourth triple-double of the season. Yes, we can say "just" there because we're used to Jokić doing that pretty much every night. While this feels like a slow start by Jokić's standards, he's still the No. 3 asset in fantasy as we're just past the first month of the season.

    Bam Adebayo: The Heat and Adebayo started off the Giannis era with four straight losses but have since gone 10-2 since Oct. 28. Adebayo is starting to find his groove on offense, averaging north of 20 points per game in November with 8.4 rebounds, 3.9 assits and nearly 3.0 stocks per contest. Other than a game in which he left early due to injury, Adebayo has at least 40 fantasy points in six straight games. Miami has a rough sledding up in Week 6 with road games against Eastern Conference rivals — the Sixers, Knicks and Cavaliers.

    It has been revealed that tyler Herro: The former Heat guard who was the centerpiece of the Giannis deal this offseason, Herro was expected to join Milwaukee and lead the team in scoring. That's been the case, though it hasn't led to much winning for the Bucks. That doesn't matter to us in fantasy, just as long as Herro is filling up the score sheet. Last Saturday, Herro scored a career-high 50 points with 11 boards and 7 assists in a close loss to Philadelphia. Milwaukee has a four-game week with some spots where Herro can showcase that scoring touch again.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has been tapped to serve as acting national cyber director while the Trump administration's permanent nominee for the role awaits Senate confirmation, a White House official told CNBC on Monday.
    • Trump had already added artificial intelligence czar to Clayton's portfolio in October.
    • The White House last week declared that President Donald Trump had picked Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to lead the Office of the National Cyber Director.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has been tapped to serve as acting national cyber director while the Trump administration's permanent nominee for the role awaits Senate confirmation, a White House official told CNBC on Monday.

    Trump had already added artificial intelligence czar to Clayton's portfolio in October. The official asked not to be named because the pick hasn't been declared.

    The White House last week declared that President Donald Trump had picked Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to lead the Office of the National Cyber Director.

    The U.S. cyber director advises the president on cybersecurity and coordinates U.S. cyber policy across federal agencies. Federal law states that a person may not serve as an acting officer if the president has submitted that person's nomination to the Senate for full appointment and if that person served as first assistant to the office for less than 90 days.

    Davies would replace Sean Cairncross, who was confirmed to the role in August 2025 and whose departure was first reported by Axios last week.

    Trump, at a White House press conference on Friday, said he decided to replace Cairncross "because I didn't think that person was good enough.".

    #153721. More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (641 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Every year, more Americans pay an extra tax levy on their investment gains — but there's still time to reduce or avoid that bill for 2026, experts say.
    • Net investment income tax, or NIIT, is a 3.8% levy on investment income once earnings exceed $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly.
    • Unlike the federal income tax or capital gains brackets, the NIIT earnings limits don't adjust annually for inflation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every year, more Americans pay an extra tax levy on their investment gains — but there's still time to reduce or avoid that bill for 2026, experts say.

    Net investment income tax, or NIIT, is a 3.8% levy on investment income once earnings exceed $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly. The tax was enacted in 2010 under President Barack Obama to help fund healthcare via the Affordable Care Act.

    Unlike the federal income tax or capital gains brackets, the NIIT earnings limits don't adjust annually for inflation.

    As a result, "more clients get hit every year," noted certified financial planner Michael Walstedt, founding advisor of Reliant Wealth Advisory in Hoboken, Upcoming Jersey.

    Roughly 5.6% of tax returns included NIIT for 2025, according to IRS data released in November for returns processed through mid-July 2026. That's up from about 3.7% for the same time frame in 2021.

    As more investors pay NIIT, here are some key things to know.

    NIIT applies when you have investment income and your earnings exceed the modified adjusted gross income, or MAGI, limits, according to certified financial planner Marianela Collado, CEO of Tobias Financial Advisors in Plantation, Florida.

    "The trick is to keep an eye on both of these numbers," said Collado, who is also a certified public accountant and member of CNBC's Financial Advisor Council.

    According to recent reports, for the NIIT earnings limit, MAGI is typically the same as adjusted gross income, or AGI. One exception would be if you have foreign income, which changes the calculation. You can find last year's AGI on line 11a of your 2025 tax return.

    Married filing jointly: $250,000.

    Married filing separately: $125,000.

    Head of household (with qualifying person): $200,000.

    Qualifying widow(er) with dependent child: $250,000.

    Recent findings suggest that NIIT applies to investment income, which includes interest, dividends, annuities, royalties, certain rents, and more. It can also include capital gains from a primary home sale, for profits that exceed the IRS exclusions. The exclusion is $250,000 for single filers or $500,000 for married couples.

    The levy stacks on top of regular income tax rates, or capital gains tax — which can be 0%, 15% or 20%, depending on earnings. That means higher earners can pay up to 23.8% on investment income, including long-term capital gains and NIIT.

    The NIIT calculation is 3.8% multiplied by the lesser of:.

    For example, if your MAGI is $30,000 above the NIIT earnings limit and you have $100,000 of investment income, you would pay 3.8% of $30,000, or $1,140.

    Alternatively, if your MAGI is $120,000 above the threshold and you have $100,000 of investment income, you would owe 3.8% of $100,000, or $3,800.

    As year-end approaches, investors should run projections to estimate their adjusted gross income, which can impact NIIT, among other tax consequences, experts say.

    If you're above the NIIT limits, you could reduce AGI by boosting pretax 401(k) deferrals or health savings account contributions, according to Collado with Tobias Financial Advisors.

    While employee 401(k) deferrals must happen by Dec. 31, you have until next year's tax deadline for health savings account contributions for 2026.

    You might also try to avoid selling assets before year-end, which could further boost AGI, experts say. Of course, any current-year tax moves should consider your long-term financial goals.

    Amid recent stock market volatility, investors may also consider so-called tax-loss harvesting, which uses losses to offset other portfolio gains, Walstedt with Reliant Wealth Advisory said.

    If your losses exceed profits, you can subtract up to $3,000 from regular income. After that, you can carry remaining losses into future tax years.

    However, if you're planning to reinvest the sale proceeds, you need to know the "wash sale rule," which blocks the tax-loss harvesting tax break for buying a "substantially identical" asset within 30 days before or after the sale.

    #153719. Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (743 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a substantial win for the manufacturer and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and remarked it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the significant indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    In a recent development, "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he said.

    Part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," mentioned JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he remarked, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan said. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the manufacturer in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he mentioned. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    Recent findings suggest that one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    #153707. ‘This establishes a bottom’: Jensen Huang’s return seen as likely to stop market sell-off, for now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (769 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘This establishes a bottom’: Jensen Huang’s return seen as likely to stop market sell-off, for now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the major averages of U.S.
    • The relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory.
    • That sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the major averages of U.S. equities surged on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, giving investors some hope that the relentless selling pressure seen last week may subside — at least temporarily.

    The relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory. The S&P alone tumbled more than 9% after Huang's departure from the chipmaker was initially confirmed on Nov. 12 through Friday.

    That sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts. But key questions linger around Nvidia and the artificial intelligence trade that has carried the bull market.

    In a recent development, "I think the AI trade is back on," noted Mark Gibbens, founder of Gibbens Capital Management. "I certainly believe this establishes a bottom and a floor in the AI trade and the recent market weakness.".

    Recent findings suggest that he added that the news likely doesn't alleviate all concerns that have driven recent declines, including worries about data center approvals after the midterms and fears that the capital expenditures cycle may have peaked. But Gibbens thinks the "keystone" role that Nvidia plays in both financing the AI buildout and the technology's supply chain means a more stable picture of the chipmaker creates a brighter view of the overall market than before.

    Sources indicate that an encouraging sign that the correction may be over came even before Nvidia's Monday announcement, according to Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management. He stated Friday's selling, which was indiscriminate and affected sectors beyond just AI-exposed companies, showed a bottom may have been building.

    Recent findings suggest that "Sometimes you just hit that crescendo where you know the market gets oversold, and I would argue that we'd be higher today, even without the Nvidia news," he said. Indeed, futures tied to the major stock indexes were broadly higher on Sunday night, before any news regarding Huang's return. "So I think that sort of signals we've likely found a place where we priced in, at least the near term, as much of the bad news that was giving markets jitters over the course of the last several weeks.".

    Strengthening the case for a bottom was that the technology sector's forward earnings valuation was cheaper than that of consumer staples, Hogan remarked. The S&P 500 consumer staples sector trades at a 20.5 multiple, per FactSet. Tech, meanwhile, trades at 16.3 times forward earnings. Hogan said that discrepancy doesn't square with the earnings outlook for the former sector.

    Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, said Huang's return created a relief rally for a market that was oversold. But he's not sure the headline alone can get the market out of its funk.

    According to recent reports, "I think the rally will probably fizzle out because now people will pull back and still have the same questions we had before he was replaced," Woods noted. Those questions will likely play out in congressional hearings, he speculated. "The market needed this jolt to get us back on our feet, but it is still a counter trend rally in an otherwise near-term downtrend.".

    Woods, though, said that the lows for the year are likely in, thanks to Friday's wash-out that spread to all sectors beyond those dependent on Nvidia's role in AI.

    Recent findings suggest that while investors celebrated Huang's return, the sell-off that accelerated after his departure started before worries about his position even began. That stemmed from concerns about financing the buildout, data center approvals after Democratic wins in the midterm elections and worries that hyperscaler capex may have already peaked or is about to.

    That's why Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, is still nervous about the "picks and shovels" companies involved in the AI trade, a group he claims includes Nvidia.

    "We should enjoy this rally, and maybe it lasts a bit, but I think that picks and shovels trade is going to be solely dependent on what that rate of capex spend is going to be," he said. "That, at the end of the day, is the story that those companies are going to have to deal with outside of bounces like we're seeing now.".

    Traders at Goldman Sachs put it more succinctly.

    "Not sure yet whether good or bad that the fate of the market is almost equal to the fate of one person. But hey ... We are not picky here," they remarked.

    — CNBC's Michelle Fox and Deena Zaidi contributed reporting.

    #153705. Breaking: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a significant buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (407 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a significant buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (407 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence company in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence company in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    Anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," noted Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, latest technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    In a recent development, the Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    Sources indicate that in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Sources indicate that ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the substantial losses.

    The fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she remarked. "That's how crazy things were.".

    #153700. Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 31%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1028 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 31%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.
    • The board of directors noted it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.
    • President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.

    The board of directors noted it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard.".

    Sources indicate that huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang.

    In a recent development, shares of Nvidia closed up 31% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6.

    "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a upcoming industrial revolution," Huang remarked in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.".

    Sources indicate that senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That enhancement prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people said.

    Recent findings suggest that huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people said. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations.

    In a recent development, trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump noted the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.".

    He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote.

    Recent findings suggest that several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected.".

    Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

    According to recent reports, for weeks following Huang's ouster, the firm's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

    Industry observers note that nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether company secrets or national security were compromised. The board said Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it.".

    "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company.".

    Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China.

    In a recent development, lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips.

    In a recent development, "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the firm's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., noted in a statement Monday.

    Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his looks to testify.

    According to recent reports, senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., noted Monday that Huang will publicly testify on Dec. 3 as the sole witness during a hearing titled, "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls.".

    "Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., a member of the Banking Committee, wrote in a post on X on Monday.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia's board has officially reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, igniting a roughly 28% relief rally into the low-$160s after last week's brutal sell-off drove shares down to $125.53. While Huang's return removes a major leadership vacuum, the stock still sits far below its $243.37 52-week high and autumn trading ranges above $200.

    Sources indicate that trapped shareholders now face a classic post-crash hurdle: heavy overhead supply. Investors who bought near prior peaks often use sharp rebounds to exit at breakeven, creating stubborn technical resistance between $175 and $210 — especially with congressional testimony and export scrutiny still lingering.

    Rather than waiting passively for a full V-shaped surge to all-time highs, underwater holders can deploy a stock repair strategy geared toward a partial recovery.

    For every 100 shares of NVDA held, an investor can overlay a January 17/195 1x2 call ratio spread for a net debit of $1.10 ($110 per lot):.

    Recent findings suggest that because elevated post-event implied volatility inflates the value of the two short $190 calls, traders can finance nearly the entire cost of the long $170 call for just $1.10 out of pocket. This structure acts as a leveraged recovery accelerator across the 175-to-195 resistance zone without adding margin risk, since one short call is covered by the existing shares and the other by the long $175 call. At January expiration, three outcomes govern the position:.

    The trade-off is capped upside above $214.90, making the strategy ideal for shareholders who view 195–215 as a realistic medium-term ceiling rather than a mere pit stop.

    #153686. Latest Update: CrowdStrike CEO defends Zscaler acquisition, calls it a 'winning combination'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (721 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: CrowdStrike CEO defends Zscaler acquisition, calls it a 'winning combination'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Monday defended the cybersecurity organization's planned acquisition of Zscaler, arguing the deal will strengthen its security capabilities and create significant growth opportunities despite a sharp sell-off in its shares.
    • According to recent reports, "When you look at the tailwinds from these agentic attacks and you listen to customers, they're looking for a complete solution and a platform that delivers not only all of the capabilities we have, but also has network visibility, protection, and control, and zero trust from a network perspective," Kurtz told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." "This is why we acquired Zscaler today.
    • Industry observers note that shares of CrowdStrike fell roughly 9% Monday after the organization announced it would acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $44 billion, raising investor concerns about dilution.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Monday defended the cybersecurity organization's planned acquisition of Zscaler, arguing the deal will strengthen its security capabilities and create significant growth opportunities despite a sharp sell-off in its shares.

    According to recent reports, "When you look at the tailwinds from these agentic attacks and you listen to customers, they're looking for a complete solution and a platform that delivers not only all of the capabilities we have, but also has network visibility, protection, and control, and zero trust from a network perspective," Kurtz told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." "This is why we acquired Zscaler today. The technology, the team, and we think it's a winning combination putting it together with the CrowdStrike platform.".

    Industry observers note that shares of CrowdStrike fell roughly 9% Monday after the organization announced it would acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $44 billion, raising investor concerns about dilution. The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Zscaler shares rose more than 17%.

    According to recent reports, the acquisition overshadowed CrowdStrike's better-than-expected quarterly results released Monday morning. The company had been scheduled to report earnings on Dec. 1, but moved up the release date to coincide with the Zscaler announcement.

    It has been revealed that the acquisition fills a key gap in CrowdStrike's cybersecurity platform. While its Falcon platform protects devices and cloud systems, Zscaler adds security across the networks connecting them. Kurtz said the deal expands CrowdStrike's addressable market by roughly $185 billion.

    CrowdStrike's largest acquisition to date comes amid a wave of consolidation in the cybersecurity industry as companies ramp up defenses against increasingly sophisticated AI-powered attacks. Recent high-profile hacks and technology outages have heightened concerns about vulnerabilities in corporate systems. CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares having soared about 96% this year entering Monday's session. For its part, Zscaler's stock ended last week down 13% year to date. As of Friday's close, the companies had a combined market value of more than $265 billion, trailing industry leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.

    Sources indicate that kurtz also highlighted the potential to sell more products across the combined customer base. He stated the companies share only about 2,000 accounts, leaving roughly 8,000 Zscaler customers that do not presently use CrowdStrike.

    Sources indicate that the companies are "very complementary overall," Kurtz said. "There's very little overlap.".

    He emphasized that the announcement generated an overwhelmingly positive response from customers.

    It has been revealed that "Most notable, customers demanded it. They loved it, and I can tell you, my phone blew up after the acquisition," Kurtz noted. "There's so many customers that love both us and Zscaler, and they're excited to see the acquisition news today.".

    To be sure, the all-stock deal has raised concerns about dilution, since CrowdStrike will concern new shares to pay for the acquisition, reducing existing shareholders' ownership stakes.

    Kurtz pushed back on those concerns, arguing that the combination will deliver immediate financial benefits. "On a free cash flow per share basis, it's immediately accretive right after close," he said. "With just modest synergies, you're going to have revenue, operating margin, and free cash flow margin accretion.".

    In a recent development, he also downplayed integration risks, pointing to the companies' longstanding technology partnership. That relationship dates back to at least 2019, and the firms announced an expanded partnership in August 2025. "Zscaler is our No. 1 technology partner," Kurtz remarked.

    In a separate "Mad Money" interview, Zscaler CEO and Founder Jay Chaudhry emphasized that combining the companies' platforms will better position them to combat a newly introduced generation of AI-powered cyberattacks.

    Recent findings suggest that "I think there's some areas where, by bringing the platforms together, we can become the best protection against AI attacks. That's why the timing became crucial, and we're coming from strength, both of us," Chaudhry said.

    #153684. Industry News: As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (440 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (440 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    In a recent development, as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    Recent findings suggest that if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the latest tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    Industry observers note that implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders major and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," remarked Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO, CNBC's Jim Cramer noted Monday.

    Recent findings suggest that "It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the "Mad Money" host said. "It's kind of a miracle given the board's insistence that he would never get the CEO job again. But it's a miracle that saved the Nasdaq which, in turn, saved the market, at least for now.".

    Nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, with both indexes posting their best days since April 2025. Monday's rebound erased nearly all of Nvidia's decline following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Before the rally Monday, the stock had fallen in all trading sessions since his departure.

    "Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one manufacturer," he said. "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary.".

    Cramer argued that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty for investors, strengthening the case for a higher valuation. The chipmaker delivered blockbuster quarterly results last week, raising its revenue growth outlook to 75%, but the results did little to stem the sell-off as investors remained concerned about its leadership.

    In a recent development, "If it weren't for the Jensen overhang, and the insistence that Jensen could never come back, ... I think the stock would have been up significantly on that quarter," Cramer noted.

    Still, Cramer cautioned that Huang's return doesn't erase the broader headwinds facing Nvidia. Growing political opposition to data center construction following the midterm elections could slow AI infrastructure expansion, while uncertainty surrounding chip sales to China threatens a potential source of demand. Meanwhile, a more hawkish Federal Reserve has pressured technology stock valuations as investors brace for higher interest rates.

    According to recent reports, those challenges, Cramer argued, make it difficult to justify a return to the $213 level Nvidia traded at before The Upcoming York Times first reported about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence on Oct. 29. But with Huang back at the helm and the company's growth outlook intact, he mentioned the stock deserves a higher valuation. The stock currently trades at roughly 10 times earnings estimates for Nvidia's fiscal 2028, according to FactSet.

    "There is just no way that, with the return of Jensen, this stock deserves the same 10 times price to earnings multiple," Cramer stated.

    Industry observers note that "These things are subjective, of course, but to start, let's say this stock deserves to trade at twelve times next year's earnings estimate, which would make this a $199 stock," Cramer noted. "That's my target.".

    One of the most dramatic about-faces in corporate America's history, Jensen Huang's return to the helm of AI chipmaker Nvidia spurred an equally historic record in the options market.More than 11 million options contracts traded on Nvidia stock Monday, the most active single day of trading for the stock's options in history. That outpaces the 9 million options traded on the Invesco QQQ Trust, and compares to 14 million traded on the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY).Despite Nvidia's monstrous 31% rally and options volume that was more than five times the 30-day average, positioning in the flows was not abnormally bullish. Of the top 10 trades by dollar amount, two massive put sales stood out, but there were no likely outright call buys, based on data from Barchart and SpotGamma. If there was speculative call-buying, it was dwarfed by big trades between the 160 and 170 strikes, where four million options traded for almost $2 billion.

    According to recent reports, nvidia closed near $165."People are mostly just trying to collect a lot of premiums through short vol trades and rolls once they heard about Jensen Huang, take advantage of the vol drop more than anything else," Jason DeLorenzo, founder of Volland, an options-analytics software, mentioned by phone. "It seems like options traders were all repricing, which created record volume, but did not create any obvious one-sidedness."Just under 6.7 million calls traded versus 4.3 million puts, according to Cboe LiveVol data. About 2.4 million calls were likely initiated by buyers, compared with 1.6 million purchasing puts, exchange data show.Open interest in calls was highest at the 170-strike, while open interest in puts was highest at the 150-strike, Barchart data show.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Fed's John Williams indicates higher interest rates likely 'over time' to address inflation

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (427 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Upcoming York Federal Reserve President John Williams noted Monday that policymakers have more work to do to bring inflation under control, though he indicated that further action can unfold over time as the economy continues to grow.
    • In a recent development, in remarks consistent with previous statements, the influential central banker expressed confidence that inflation will get closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027 before hitting the goal the following year.
    • Industry observers note that "But getting inflation back to 2% is 100% essential," he mentioned in remarks at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Upcoming York Federal Reserve President John Williams noted Monday that policymakers have more work to do to bring inflation under control, though he indicated that further action can unfold over time as the economy continues to grow.

    In a recent development, in remarks consistent with previous statements, the influential central banker expressed confidence that inflation will get closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027 before hitting the goal the following year. He also said that while artificial intelligence is pressuring prices, there's "little evidence" it will be the source of more persistent inflation.

    Industry observers note that "But getting inflation back to 2% is 100% essential," he mentioned in remarks at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York. "We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis. There is still work to do to get that done.".

    The comments come at a delicate moment for monetary policy, as the economy continues to grow and inflation stays well above the Fed's goal.

    Fed officials have differed over how quickly to raise rates, with some advocating more aggressive action while others, including Williams, have emphasized a measured approach.

    It has been revealed that williams ascribed the current inflation pressures to the conflict in Iran, demand for goods associated with the AI build-out and tariffs, the effects of which he remarked "have largely abated" as a source of pressure. Nevertheless, he expressed confidence that inflation will subside substantially in 2027 even as economic growth remains robust and unemployment edges lower.

    The Federal Open Market Committee next meets on Dec. 8-9, with markets fully pricing in a quarter percentage point interest rate increase from the current target range of 3.75%-4%. The remarks from Williams are expected to be the last major policy statement from any Fed official before the December decision.

    "Monetary policy cannot move ships or reopen pipelines and refineries, but it can — and must — ensure that these shocks do not lead to broader or persistent inflationary dynamics or erode well-anchored inflation expectations," Williams said, according to his prepared remarks.

    Williams did not explicitly address the December meeting expectations, instead pointing to the statement released after the prior FOMC meeting in late October that said the "accumulation of more information" will help decide the future policy path.

    "The data that we have received since then show that the economy has remained strong and that inflation has continued to run too high," he stated.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • In a recent development, on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    In a recent development, on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note noted.

    Sources indicate that the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    In that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    #153654. Industry News: Amazon faces FAA probe after delivery drone strikes Michigan fiber cable, garage

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (395 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Amazon faces FAA probe after delivery drone strikes Michigan fiber cable, garage

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (395 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Federal Aviation Administration mentioned Monday it will investigate a recent Amazon drone crash near Detroit.
    • On Friday, one of Amazon's MK30 drones "landed on a resident's garage" during a delivery in Huntington Woods, Michigan, a suburb north of Detroit, Amazon spokesperson Jack Stelzner told CNBC in a statement.
    • According to recent reports, the crash occurred after the drone dropped off a customer's shampoo order around 4:30 p.m.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Aviation Administration mentioned Monday it will investigate a recent Amazon drone crash near Detroit.

    On Friday, one of Amazon's MK30 drones "landed on a resident's garage" during a delivery in Huntington Woods, Michigan, a suburb north of Detroit, Amazon spokesperson Jack Stelzner told CNBC in a statement.

    According to recent reports, the crash occurred after the drone dropped off a customer's shampoo order around 4:30 p.m. local time, and one of its propellers was damaged in the incident, according to ABC affiliate WXYZ.

    A preliminary incident report posted to the FAA's website states the drone "struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff." The report claims the condition of the drone is unknown.

    Stelzner said there were no injuries, the drone has been removed and Amazon is in contact with the resident.

    In a recent development, "Safety is our top priority and incidents are extremely rare," Stelzner stated. "Anytime a delivery does not go as planned we investigate what happened and use the findings to further improve the service.".

    An FAA spokesperson confirmed it's investigating the incident. A spokesperson for the National Transportation Safety Board, a federal agency that also investigates aviation accidents, mentioned it's aware of the incident and is continuing to gather information. The agency hasn't yet determined whether it will open a probe, the NTSB spokesperson added.

    Industry observers note that amazon has been working to make widespread drone delivery a reality ever since founder Jeff Bezos laid out his vision for the program nearly 13 years ago. The rollout has been slow, as the program encountered regulatory delays and staff cuts, as well as technical challenges and pushback from some communities where it conducted early pilots.

    Sources indicate that expansion has recently ramped up. The company is targeting a launch of its drone service in 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of the year, while an Amazon executive claimed it has the "highest demand drone delivery service in the industry," CNBC previously reported.

    The e-commerce giant has encountered some challenges along the way. Federal investigators opened a probe nearly one year ago after an Amazon drone downed an internet cable in Waco, Texas. One month earlier, a separate federal probe was opened into an incident near Phoenix, where two Amazon drones collided with a construction crane.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (915 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: AI race spreads from robots to smartphones

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing.
    • I'm just back from APEC in Shenzhen, where I saw the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia gather along with other member economies.
    • It only took a few months for a humanoid robot to get better at picking up household items.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses.

    I'm just back from APEC in Shenzhen, where I saw the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia gather along with other member economies. Beneath the fanfare, what's changed on the tech front in what's often dubbed China's Silicon Valley?

    It only took a few months for a humanoid robot to get better at picking up household items.

    Sources indicate that even after a human knocked a box and toys away from their original spots, a LimX robot quickly located them and moved them to pre-set locations. While still far from perfect, the smoothness of the demo contrasted with the robot's more stilted movements I'd seen early this summer — and inability then to react to rapid changes in tasks.

    When we caught up in Shenzhen last week, CFO Jesse Liu declined to comment on LimX's IPO prepares. But he told me that his conversations around the APEC CEO Summit revealed an excitement around a fresh development for humanoids: growing demand for robot chips that can run smarter large language models locally, instead of on the cloud.

    "A lot of chipmakers are now happy about the latest developments in LLMs because they think robotic OEMs will actually begin to integrate more storage, and reasoning, and compute, and inference infrastructure on the edge, or locally inside the robot body," Liu noted, referring to original equipment manufacturers.

    "They do see robots moving from hundreds of units to thousands of units, to tens of thousands of units, beginning to enter that kind of automotive quantity," he noted, pointing to chip suppliers such as Horizon Robotics.

    New AI models, particularly GPT-6 Astra, have shown not just improved reasoning, but better control of robots.

    Industry observers note that that puts more of the onus on hardware makers, for robots or other devices, to create practical applications. LimX mentioned it's working with business partners in over 30 markets, including Switzerland where the robots serve as power plant inspectors in rural areas.

    Sources indicate that the key for powering AI's transition into the physical world is on-device chips and more powerful batteries. That means Nvidia's most expensive, cutting-edge chips won't be the only ones powering generative AI models.

    So far, even in basic consumer applications such as smartphones, AI isn't transformative enough to be a top-three selling point for mass-market people, Thomas Bai, AI product expert at smartphone firm Honor, told me in Shenzhen.

    He expects that in the next few years, as smartphone chips are able to run more powerful AI models, the "super agent" tech can become better at completing tasks on its own, and anticipating a user's needs — such as ordering coffee.

    It has been revealed that counterpoint on Nov. 19 forecast that in the retail industry, "edge AI" revenue will surge sixfold by 2032, with roughly half of revenue coming from retail robots that clean and check inventory — often with the help of smaller AI models that can run on locally embedded chips.

    But more capable, on-device AI also requires more battery power, Honor's Bai pointed out.

    Honor's X70 Android smartphone, which debuted last summer, boasts a battery with 8,300 milliampere-hours for a total device weight of just under 200 grams. That compares with 5,000 mAH for the 214-gram flagship Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, and roughly 5,400 mAH for this year's 249-gram Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max, according to GSM Arena.

    LimX's Oli humanoid comes with 9,500 mAH battery capacity, lasting the robot about 1.5 hours.

    Such AI applications, however, remain sensitive to the memory-chip shortage weighing on the industry.

    The X70 was the best-selling Android phone in the entry to mid-tier range, stated Shenzhen-based Counterpoint analyst Shiwen Ma.

    While Ma remarked penetration of smartphones with generative AI features is higher in China at 55% versus 38% overseas, the offerings are still not essential to people, while rising memory-chip costs make it harder for manufacturers to bring AI-powered devices to the mass market.

    Geely-backed automotive tech tech giant EcarX's CFO Dylan Jeng told me earlier this month he expects the memory price surge to persist through 2027, and even the first half of 2028.

    The chipmaker that can narrow the gap for on-device AI needs could find its moment soon.

    Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged.

    Industry observers note that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke exclusively on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." President Donald Trump on Friday stated he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week.

    How China is using summits to expand its global influence.

    For a second year in a row, Xi has brought Russian President Vladimir Putin together with another major world leader on mainland Chinese shores. But U.S.-China trade, Taiwan and tech tensions remain unresolved as Trump returned from Asia.

    Putin scores 'massive win' at first trilateral meeting.

    Recent findings suggest that the first-ever three-way summit is "arguably a diplomatic victory for Moscow," stated Andrius Tursa, an advisor for Central and Eastern Europe and Russia at Teneo. The view from inside the APEC welcome banquet showed the leaders were in close proximity from the start of the summit.

    Nov. 27 - Dec. 6: Guangzhou auto show.
